COURT'S OR JUDGE'S ORDERS
WPSS No.1588 of 2026
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Amar Murti Shukla, learned Counsel for
petitioner.
2. Mr. Ganga Singh Negi, learned Addl. CSC for the
State.
3. The petitioner has filed the present petition
seeking a direction to the respondents to pay arrears of
salary including balance retiral dues of the petitioner
within a stipulated time.
4. The petitioner retired from the post of Head
Master, Junior High School on 31.07.2016. Some of
the arrears of salary as well as some retiral dues have
already been paid to the petitioner. The petitioner
contends that balance of arrears of salary and retiral
dues are pending with the respondent department.
The petitioner contends that earlier he moved a
representation to the respondent no.4 but no decision
has been taken by the respondent no.4 in the
representation of the petitioner. The petitioner is
therefore before this Court.
5. The petitioner contends that this Court may take
cognizance on the matter that the petitioner retired in
the year 2016, and may direct the respondents to
decide the representation pending disposal with the
respondent authority.
6. Since the representation is not annexed with the
writ petition and further the date of the representation
is not pleaded in the writ petition, therefore, it would

be conducive in the interest of justice that the
petitioner be given liberty to file a fresh representation
ventilating his grievance therein and the respondent
no.4 is directed to decide the said representation
within a stipulated time.
7. Learned counsel for the State does not have any
objection if such an order is passed by this Court.
8. The writ petition is finally disposed of. It is
provided that the petitioner shall file a representation
within a period of 15 days from today ventilating his
grievance in detail and if such representation is filed by
the petitioner within 15 days, the respondent no.4
shall decide the same within eight weeks thereafter by
a speaking and reasoned order strictly in accordance
with law after satisfying itself about the entitlement of
the petitioner.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 17.06.2026 R.Dang
